questions: Did these abnormal postures begin suddenly?
Have they progressively worsened over time?
Are the postures or movements involuntary?
Do they become worse when you try to move, walk, speak, or perform a task?
Do they improve temporarily when you touch the affected body part or change position?
Do the abnormal movements or postures disappear completely during sleep?
Did the symptoms begin after taking an antipsychotic, anti-nausea medicine, antidepressant, or other new medication?
Have you ever had a similar episode before?
Were your early development, walking, and school performance normal?
Have you ever had seizures or episodes of loss of awareness?
Have you had difficulty speaking or swallowing?
Have you had tremor, slowness, or stiffness in addition to the abnormal postures?
Have you had muscle weakness or loss of sensation?
Have you had abdominal pain, yellowing of the eyes, dark urine, or easy bruising?
Have you experienced recent personality change, depression, irritability, or other psychiatric symptoms?
Have you injured yourself intentionally or unintentionally because of involuntary movements?
Does anyone in your family have abnormal movements, tremor, seizures, or similar posturing?
Was there a difficult birth, premature delivery, or serious illness affecting your brain during childhood?
Have you had recent fever, infection, toxin exposure, or head injury?
Do you have pain in your neck, back, arms, or legs because of these postures?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Juvenile/adult-onset (type III) GM1 gangliosidosis due to biallelic pathogenic GLB1 variants causing lysosomal β-galactosidase deficiency

Alternative: Dystonia due to another inherited neurodegenerative disorder, particularly neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA)

Alternative: Juvenile-onset Huntington disease or another hereditary chorea–dystonia syndrome

Alternative: Primary genetic generalized dystonia unrelated to GLB1 variants
